makefile_edits: The upstream emscripten platform block emitted only an intermediate LLVM bitcode archive (.bc). It performs the full Emscripten link to <profile>.js + .wasm with CC=emcc/CXX=em++/LD=em++, STATIC_LINKING=0, and the raw-libretro flag set (ALLOW_TABLE_GROWTH, exported runtime methods incl. addFunction, exported retro_*). This follow-up added: (1) -s ASYNCIFY=1 -s ASYNCIFY_STACK_SIZE=1048576 so retro_run yields to the browser and returns instead of hanging in bsnes's libco scheduler; (2) per-PROFILE DISTINCT output filename + MODULARIZE EXPORT_NAME (bsnes_accuracy / bsnes_performance) so both cores can coexist without a symbol collision; (3) -s EXPORT_ES6=1 so each core is an ES6 default-export factory that core-loader.js resolves via dynamic import.
libco_backend_edit: libco defaults to the sjlj (setjmp/longjmp) backend under Emscripten, whose raw-stack context switches ASYNCIFY cannot unwind (retro_run hang). Added libco/emscripten.c, an Emscripten Fibers (emscripten_fiber_*) libco backend, and wired it in libco/libco.c under the __EMSCRIPTEN__ target so cothread switches cooperate with ASYNCIFY.
verified_with: node tools/run-smoke.mjs cores/<profile>.js 12 — for BOTH profiles: retro_load_game()==true, retro_run() RETURNS within a bounded wall clock (no hang), video_refresh fires with a non-null framebuffer, and the frame counter advances across the run. Note: the harness re-execs Node with --liftoff-only to avoid a Node/V8 TurboFan codegen crash (IdField::is_valid) when JIT-optimizing these large ASYNCIFY WASM modules — a Node-side JIT limit, not a core defect (browsers do not hit it).
